name: Alma

lifecycle.notes: Acquired by Spring Health (closed May 2026); operates as Alma, part of Spring Health.

short_description: Paid-membership network that credentials licensed clinicians with insurers, bills on their behalf, and includes practice tools and telehealth.
long_description: Alma credentials licensed clinicians with insurers (new members must join at least one of Aetna, Cigna or Optum), submits claims and pays out within about two weeks of submission. Unlike Headway or Grow, clinicians pay a membership: $95/month billed annually ($1,140/year), more if billed monthly. Membership includes practice tools, telehealth and AI-assisted notes, and clinicians keep their own practice identity. Alma accepts fully licensed clinicians only. Spring Health completed its acquisition of Alma in May 2026; Alma says provider fees and contracts did not change.
one_liner: In-network credentialing and billing for a flat membership, with your practice still your own.
best_for: Licensed clinicians who want insurance panels without credentialing themselves
Clinicians who want billing, an EHR and telehealth for one flat fee
Clinicians who want to keep their own practice identity rather than a platform brand
Prescribers (NPs, MDs) as well as therapists
not_for: Clinicians who want a no-fee network (Headway, Grow and Rula do not charge a membership)
Very low caseloads, where $1,140 a year may not pay off

notes.insurance-billing: Credentialing and claims for a $95/month membership (billed annually), rather than a share of each session.
notes.solo-therapist: You keep your own practice identity, and the membership includes notes, telehealth and a client directory.

pricing.notes: $1,140/year billed annually; monthly billing costs more. Sales tax may apply.

seo.title: Alma: Insurance Credentialing + AI Notes for Therapists
seo.meta_description: Alma offers insurance credentialing, AI notes, EHR, and billing for therapists at $125/month. Higher negotiated rates, weekly payments. Acquired by Spring...

faqs.q: How much does Alma cost for therapists?
faqs.a: Alma costs $125/month or $95/month when billed annually ($1,140/year). No free trial. You keep 100% of reimbursements (unlike revenue-sharing platforms). The fee is owed monthly regardless of caseload—factor this into your breakeven calculation.

faqs.q: How fast is credentialing through Alma?
faqs.a: Alma credentials therapists in under 45 days—3x faster than solo credentialing. However, these credentials belong to Alma. If you leave, you must re-credential independently (60-120 day process with potential income gap).

faqs.q: Does Alma negotiate higher reimbursement rates?
faqs.a: Alma claims to negotiate $10-30 higher rates than solo credentialing. However, late 2024 Optum rate cuts affected Alma providers significantly. Platform-negotiated rates can change without your input.

faqs.q: What happened with Optum rates in 2024?
faqs.a: In November 2024, Optum/UHC implemented rate cuts that reduced some Alma provider reimbursements. Because Alma negotiates on your behalf, providers had no direct say in these changes—a key tradeoff of platform credentialing.

faqs.q: Does Alma's AI notes work for in-person sessions?
faqs.a: No. Alma's AI notes only work for telehealth video sessions conducted through their platform. In-person therapists won't benefit from this feature and would need a separate AI scribe solution.

faqs.q: What happens if I leave Alma?
faqs.a: Your insurance credentials stay with Alma. You'd need to re-credential independently (60-120 days). Clients may or may not follow—those who found you via Alma's directory might simply find another in-network provider.

faqs.q: How does Alma compare to Headway and Grow?
faqs.a: Alma charges $125/month flat while Headway and Grow take undisclosed revenue cuts. Alma includes EHR and AI notes (video only). All three experienced 2024 Optum cuts. None give you portable credentials. Alma pays weekly; Headway bi-weekly; Grow weekly.
